title: Location, Map, Route & Scene Binding
objective: Extend the prepared MAS Adventure workspace with deterministic Location, Map, Route and Scene Binding over the MAS-01..10 foundations while preserving canonical Location/Map/Scene/route/spatial owner authority and keeping prepared bindings distinct from live world, scene or navigation mutation.

scope.purpose: Represent prepared Location, Map, Route and Scene bindings inside the MAS workspace without turning bindings into canonical spatial, map, navigation or live Scene mutation.
scope.completion_gate: A representative MAS workspace can deterministically bind prepared location, map, route and Scene references over the completed MAS foundations with explicit references and fail-closed invalid states while preserving canonical owner authority and never treating prepared bindings as executed live world, navigation or Scene truth.

selection_boundaries: Existing MAS validation family remains active; no family transition is authorized or required.
MAS-01 through MAS-10 remain completed foundations and are not reopened silently.

Location, Map, Route and Scene bindings are prepared binding semantics only; canonical Location/World, MCS/map-cartography, route/navigation, Scene and Action/Event/runtime owners retain live spatial, navigation, scene-state and mutation authority.
A prepared binding never proves a world location changed, a route was traversed, a map/cartography record mutated, a Scene became live or an Action/Event occurred.
Detailed MAS-11 owner/spatial seams are loaded only inside this tranche and unresolved references fail closed.
MAS-12 retains Character, Creature, Token, Portrait & Cast Presentation Binding scope and must not be pulled forward.
CNI-12 and PCA remain unselected; MAS-12+ and SMB-08 remain unauthorized.
next_action: On the authorized application branch, load only MAS-10 plus targeted MCS/map/location/Scene/route/spatial owner seams, establish causal MAS-11 RED, then implement the minimum deterministic prepared binding contract without pulling MAS-12 presentation binding forward.
